subject: SLA carveout request: Aurora Labs private VPC (peer egress responsibility)
messages:
From: John Park <john.park@auroralabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@auroralabs.com, security@auroralabs.com
Date: 2025-06-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLA carveout for Aurora Labs private VPC deployment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo on Friday. Aurora is preparing to deploy Redwood into our private VPC in our Azure tenancy, and our infra team has flagged one item that will require an SLA carveout. We control the peering, egress NAT, and last-mile transit; intermittent packet loss and peering flaps on our side have historically introduced latencies beyond what Redwood measures in the colocated environment. For compliance we need the contract to reflect that any availability or latency impact caused by customer-controlled peering or our managed transit providers will not count against Redwood uptime SLOs, and that latency credits (if any) will be limited to the Redwood-controlled path.

Can you provide the language your team typically uses for: 1) a shared-responsibility matrix that names 'customer-managed peering/transit' as excluded; 2) telemetry/diagnostic data Redwood would require to validate incidents that appear to be on our side; and 3) an evidence exchange process (logs, traceroutes) with a timebox?

Attached: network-diagram.pdf (diagram, 245 KB)

Our legal/security colleagues are looped in (cc). We'd like to get a mutual draft to feed into our procurement cycle this week.

Thanks,
John Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurora Labs
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@auroralabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for Aurora Labs private VPC deployment

John — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram, that helps. Quick answers up front: we can accept a narrow carveout for customer-controlled peering/transit, but we need (a) a named shared-responsibility matrix in the SOW, (b) continuous access to the request-level telemetry (request ids + route metadata) for a 30-day window after incidents, and (c) an agreed evidence exchange SLA (72 hours for initial packet captures/traceroutes on either side).

Would you be open to a short call today or tomorrow to align on the exact exclusion wording? I’m copying Laura (legal/ops) and Priyom (account lead) and Karthik (SRE policy) so we can put together a draft.

Proposed next step: we’ll circulate a one-page carveout appendix and a draft SOW clause; if that looks good we can route it for signature via DocuSign.

Best,
Soojín Lee (she/her)
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-12T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: draft language for Aurora carveout (doc attached)

Team — pulling together language now. Key items I recommend we include in the appendix:

- Definitions: 'Customer Network Boundary' (explicit CIDR ranges / peering endpoints) and 'Redwood-Controlled Path' (the infra between Redwood inference nodes and the peering interface).
- Exclusion: "Availability and latency SLOs do not apply to incidents where causal evidence shows root cause is within the Customer Network Boundary, including customer-managed peering, NAT egress, or third-party transit providers."
- Evidence exchange: initial packet captures/traceroutes within 72 hours; both parties must provide signed attestations of time ranges for captured data.
- Telemetry access: request id logs (tokenized), timestamps, and ASN-level hop lists for 30 days post-incident.
- Fallback/mitigation: Redwood will offer automatic fallback to an alternative region/model where feasible; such fallbacks may incur different cost/latency profiles.
- Audit: during PoC period Redwood will run joint diagnostics once per major release to verify boundary assumptions.

I attached a starter SOW appendix (sow-vpc-exception-draft.docx). We should keep the exclusion tight — avoid an open-ended "third-party transit" carveout unless Aurora can list providers and peering points. If Priyom can confirm the critical peering endpoints and whether they plan to use transient carriers, we can finalize.

-Laura
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
